How to Set Up Team Permissions

Last updated: February 20, 2025 | Written by Meridian Support Team

Applies to: Professional and Enterprise plans

Team permissions let you control who can view, edit, and manage projects within your Meridian workspace. This guide walks you through configuring roles and access levels so every team member has the right level of access.

Prerequisites

Before you begin, make sure you have the following:

  • A Meridian workspace on the Professional or Enterprise plan.
  • Admin role in your workspace (only admins can manage permissions).
  • At least one team member already invited to your workspace.
Note: Starter plan workspaces use a simplified permission model where all members have equal edit access. Upgrade to Professional or Enterprise to unlock role-based permissions.

Understanding Roles

Meridian includes three built-in roles. Enterprise customers can also create custom roles with granular permissions.

Role Can View Can Edit Can Manage
AdminAll projectsAll projectsWorkspace settings, billing, members
MemberAssigned projectsAssigned projectsOwn tasks and comments only
ViewerAssigned projectsNoNo

Step-by-Step Setup

Step 1: Open Workspace Settings

Click your workspace name in the top-left corner of the dashboard, then select Settings from the dropdown menu. Navigate to the Members & Permissions tab in the left sidebar.

Step 2: Review Current Members

You will see a list of all workspace members with their current role displayed next to their name. Review this list to identify any members whose access needs to change. New members default to the Member role when they accept their invitation.

Step 3: Assign Roles

Click the role badge next to any member's name to open the role selector. Choose the appropriate role from the dropdown: Admin, Member, or Viewer. The change takes effect immediately — the member will see updated access the next time they load a page.

Tip: Keep the number of Admin users to a minimum. We recommend having two to three admins per workspace for redundancy without over-exposing sensitive settings.

Step 4: Set Project-Level Permissions

For more granular control, open any project and go to Project Settings > Access. Here you can override workspace-level roles for specific projects. For example, you can grant a Viewer edit access to a single project without changing their workspace-wide role. You can also restrict a Member from accessing certain confidential projects.

Warning: Project-level overrides take precedence over workspace roles. If a member has conflicting permissions, the project-level setting wins. Document your overrides to avoid confusion during team changes.

Step 5: Create Teams (Optional)

If your workspace has many members, organize them into teams. Go to Settings > Teams and click Create Team. Give the team a name (for example, "Engineering" or "Marketing"), add members, and then assign the team to projects. When you assign a team to a project, all team members inherit the specified role for that project. This is much faster than assigning permissions individually when you have large groups.

Verifying Permissions

After configuring roles, verify the setup by reviewing the Access Audit Log in Settings > Security. This log shows every permission change with timestamps and the admin who made the change. You can also ask a team member to confirm their view by navigating to the workspace — they should only see projects they have been granted access to.

Troubleshooting

  • Member cannot see a project: Check that the member is either directly assigned to the project or belongs to a team with project access.
  • Member can edit when they should only view: Check for project-level overrides that may grant higher permissions than the workspace role.
  • Cannot change a member's role: Only workspace Admins can modify roles. Confirm your own role in Settings > Members.

If you need further assistance, contact our support team at hello@meridian.digital or use the live chat during business hours.
